test.name: A search-hit review spawns one evaluate-search-results per named hit and offers the Matches
test.description: Issue #3522, research/SKILL.md "Search-hit review". The user names three hits of the full-text search log_008. The router reads results/log_008.json#hits, spawns one @plugin:evaluate-search-results per named hit with projectPath, the row's ref as hitRef and a target, relays each verdict, and ends "Continue with extracting the 3 Matches?". evaluate-search-results is stubbed with one canned return for every spawn: verdict match, alreadyExtracted false, and no hitRef line, because one text answers every spawn and a hitRef line would name the wrong hit; the router pairs each return with its spawn. So the offer's count is the spawn count. Hits 2, 4 and 7, not hit 1: hit 1 (3QSQ-G9WC-F61H) is already extracted as src_005, so a canned alreadyExtracted false would contradict project_context. Asserted from the hook records by test_search_hit_review_spawns_one_agent_per_hit (reviews-search-hits, reviews-hits:log_008:2,4,7), which the judge cannot see.

verdict: match

The evaluator labelled this hit a Match. It holds a detail the tree does not have yet.

judge_context: This is a ROUTING test of research/SKILL.md's "Search-hit review". The spawns are asserted deterministically from the hook records (test_routes_to_expected_skill, test_search_hit_review_spawns_one_agent_per_hit): one evaluate-search-results spawn per named hit, each naming projectPath, its own hitRef and a target, and a last line "Continue with extracting the 3 Matches?". You cannot see the spawns. Do not grade them.

evaluate-search-results is STUBBED with one canned return for every hit: a Match, not yet extracted, with the same two-sentence summary. Every hit therefore comes back a Match in identical words. That is the stub, not a defect of the router, and nothing is written to the project. The stub gives that Match even to a hit whose title plainly cannot be Iram Hyde: hit 7 of log_008 is a 1664 English will. Relaying that Match is correct and is NOT a factual error; do not grade whether a relayed verdict is plausible.

The router judges nothing from the hit list itself and extracts nothing in this turn: it relays each verdict and offers the extraction. Saying from a hit's title whether it is Iram Hyde, or extracting a hit in this turn, is the failure.

PROJECT_LIST FIRST IS REQUIRED. When no projectPath is named, the router's first call is project_list with no arguments, to find the project. Its folder answer is the live tool's real answer, not an error.
